subject: community-medicine
title: Hepatitis B: Serology, Window Period and Prevention

steps.title: Endemicity is read off HBsAg prevalence
steps.tx: **HBsAg prevalence** grades endemicity: 8 percent or more in the general population defines high endemicity, 5 to 7 high-intermediate, 2 to 4 low-intermediate, and under 2 percent low endemicity. India sits in the intermediate bands in programme teaching. The grade decides how aggressively birth dose and catch-up vaccination must be pushed.
steps.say: One blood marker grades whole regions. Eight percent surface antigen or more means high endemicity; under two means low. Intermediate grades, India's teaching position, demand strong birth dose discipline without complacency.

steps.title: Three antigens, three antibodies
steps.tx: The virus presents **surface antigen (HBsAg)**, core antigen (HBcAg, not free in blood) and e antigen (HBeAg), answered by anti-HBs, anti-HBc and anti-HBe. Every serology stem is a pattern of these six. Surface antibody alone means vaccine immunity; core antibody presence proves natural infection happened at some point.
steps.say: Six markers, every stem a pattern. Surface antigen means infected now; surface antibody means protected; core antibody proves natural infection once occurred; e antigen flags heavy replication. Learn the grammar before the sentences.

steps.title: The serology timeline and window period
steps.tx: The timeline chart shows **HBsAg rising first**, followed by HBeAg and symptoms, then IgM anti-HBc, with anti-HBs appearing only after HBsAg clears. Between surface antigen loss and antibody gain lies the window period, when IgM anti-HBc alone proves acute infection. Chronic persistence insets at the right when HBsAg survives beyond 6 months.
steps.say: Read the curves in order. Surface antigen first, e antigen with symptoms, core IgM next, surface antibody last after clearance. The gap between antigen loss and antibody gain is the window, provable only by core IgM.

vis.caption: Acute hepatitis B marker curves, window period and chronic persistence. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.title: Pattern table examiners actually use
steps.tx: **Acute hepatitis B** reads HBsAg positive, IgM anti-HBc positive, HBeAg positive. Chronic active replication keeps HBsAg and IgG anti-HBc with HBeAg; low replication swaps in anti-HBe. Vaccinated persons show anti-HBs alone. Window period shows IgM anti-HBc alone. Four rows answer nearly every serology stem written.
steps.say: Four rows answer nearly every stem. Acute: surface antigen plus core IgM. Chronic replicating: add e antigen. Vaccinated: surface antibody alone. Window: core IgM alone. Drill the table, not trivia.

steps.title: Age decides chronicity
steps.tx: **Perinatal infection** becomes chronic in up to 90 percent of infected newborns, childhood infection in roughly a third, and immunocompetent adult infection in under 5 percent. That gradient is the entire public health argument for the 24-hour birth dose: the same virus is a brief illness in adults and a lifelong carrier state from birth.
steps.say: Age writes the prognosis. Nine of ten infected newborns carry for life; fewer than one in twenty adults do. The twenty four hour birth dose exists because of that single gradient.

steps.tx: **Perinatal infection** with hepatitis B becomes chronic in up to ninety percent of infected newborns. Childhood infection becomes chronic in roughly a third. Immunocompetent adult infection becomes chronic in under five percent. That age gradient is the public health argument for a birth dose within twenty four hours. The same virus is usually a brief illness in adults and a lifelong carrier state when acquired at birth.
steps.say: Hepatitis B carriage follows age. Up to nine in ten infected newborns stay chronic, about a third of children do, and fewer than one in twenty healthy adults do. The twenty four hour birth dose exists because of that gradient.

vis.alt: A bar chart shows chronic hepatitis B in about ninety percent of perinatal infections, about thirty percent of childhood infections, and under five percent of adult infections.
vis.caption: Bars compare lifelong carriage after hepatitis B acquired at birth, in childhood, and in adult life. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Prevention: vaccine, HBIG, blood safety
steps.tx: **Prevention stacks** three layers: universal infant vaccination with birth dose, hepatitis B immunoglobulin plus vaccine within hours for babies of carrier mothers and after needle-stick exposure, and screened blood with safe injection practice. Post-exposure management is time-critical in hours, not clinic visits, a distinction stems test with occupational exposure stories.
steps.say: Three layers prevent. Universal infant vaccine with its birth dose, immunoglobulin plus vaccine within hours after exposure or carrier-mother birth, and screened blood with safe injections. Post-exposure clocks run in hours.

steps.title: National hepatitis control and free treatment
steps.tx: The **national viral hepatitis programme** integrates testing at facilities (HBsAg in antenatal panels), model treatment centres giving free oral antivirals, and Haryana's free test-and-treat model for hepatitis C adopted nationally. Tenofovir-based therapy suppresses hepatitis B without curing carriage, so prevention by vaccine remains the programme's foundation stone.
steps.say: Programmes now test and treat free. Antenatal surface antigen screening, model treatment centres, oral antivirals that suppress without curing. Suppression is not eradication, so the birth dose remains the foundation stone.

steps.title: Needle-stick: the occupational stem
steps.tx: After **needle-stick exposure** from an HBsAg-positive source, an unvaccinated worker receives HBIG and starts vaccine immediately; a vaccinated responder (anti-HBs 10 mIU/ml or more) needs nothing; a known non-responder gets HBIG with booster logic per protocol. The stem always hides vaccination and responder status inside the story; extract both before answering.
steps.say: Occupational stems hide two facts. Vaccination history and responder status decide everything: immunoglobulin plus vaccine for the unvaccinated, nothing for proven responders, protocol cover for non-responders. Extract both facts before answering.

steps.title: Counselling carriers without stigma
steps.tx: **Carrier counselling** covers household vaccination, not sharing razors or toothbrushes, safe sex until partners immunise, blood donation exclusion, and reassurance that casual contact, food sharing and work do not transmit. Alcohol avoidance and periodic liver monitoring complete chronic care. Stigma, not infectivity, is usually the heavier daily burden services must treat.
steps.say: Counselling protects households without exiling people. Vaccinate contacts, separate razors, defer blood donation, reassure on food and work. Add liver monitoring and alcohol avoidance. Stigma usually outweighs infectivity as daily burden.
